# A PR opened through a tool can carry an attribution footer you didn't write

**What happened (2026-10-03, ADR 0073 P2-A stack, #1153/#1154).** PRs opened
through the GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` tool were published with a
"Generated by Claude Code" footer and a session link appended server-side,
although the submitted body had none. This violates the repo rule that PR
bodies carry no AI attribution (root `CLAUDE.md`, Conventions).

**Rule.** After opening a PR through any tool, re-read the published body
(`pull_request_read get`) and strip any footer that tool added. An
`update_pull_request` with the clean body removes it, and the edit sticks.
Check commit messages the same way (`git log -1 --format=%B`) before
pushing: no `Claude-Session:` or `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.

**Why it generalizes.** Tooling can inject content outside what you
submitted. "I didn't write it" isn't "it isn't there", so verify the
published artifact, not the request you sent.
